claims.claim: Lean supports custom syntax categories, source information and command elaboration needed for a dedicated program DSL.
claims.impact: Use a custom command elaborator instead of encoding the DSL as an unrestricted Lean StateM builder.

claims.claim: ProofForge V2 has one user-level program declaration and no user-written execution kind.
claims.impact: Target selection performs materialization; requirements are inferred from semantics.

claims.claim: EVM execution is a transaction-based shared-state machine with account code and persistent per-account storage.
claims.impact: EvmPlan owns storage layout, ABI, call and revert lowering.

claims.claim: Solana programs receive explicitly supplied accounts whose owner and data permissions constrain mutation.
claims.impact: SolanaPlan requires an account schema, signer/writable constraints and CPI metadata.

claims.claim: NEAR cross-contract calls create asynchronous promises/receipts rather than EVM-style synchronous nested calls.
claims.impact: NearPlan must model promise DAGs and receipt-local commit boundaries.

claims.claim: NEAR contract preparation rejects a Wasm function with more than 50000 locals.
claims.impact: NearPlan and its typed recipe must bound generated locals per exported method before rendering Wasm.

claims.claim: CosmWasm is a Cosmos SDK contract environment with messages, IBC integration and instance-scoped state, not generic Wasm semantics.
claims.impact: CosmWasmPlan remains separate from all other Wasm host plans.

claims.claim: Exact submessage/reply savepoint and rollback behavior must be pinned to a versioned CosmWasm runtime profile before implementation.
claims.impact: The CosmWasm backend is design-only in Phase 1.

claims.claim: Soroban distinguishes instance, persistent and temporary storage and couples entries to TTL/archival behavior.
claims.impact: SorobanPlan must make durability and TTL policy explicit.

claims.claim: Soroban authorization is expressed through address authentication and invocation trees, not merely a caller scalar.
claims.impact: Authority requirements cannot be collapsed into context.caller.

claims.claim: ICP canisters are Wasm actors with System API imports, Candid interfaces, stable memory and message-level commit boundaries.
claims.impact: IcpPlan owns actor methods, Candid, cycles and await boundaries.

claims.claim: Wasm is an artifact encoding and instruction format; it does not determine state, authorization, call, commit or upgrade semantics.
claims.impact: Share only Wasm AST/encoding and structural validation; keep four host plans.

claims.claim: Noir produces a circuit/witness workflow and delegates proof generation to a backend; it has no native persistent chain state.
claims.impact: Noir materializes a state transition relation with external continuity, not a deployable contract.

claims.claim: Unconstrained Noir execution is not automatically constrained by the proof system.
claims.impact: Phase 1 rejects unconstrained/foreign-oracle lowering unless a separate soundness proof is accepted.

claims.claim: Noir native u64 inputs are range-constrained fixed-width integers and live ordinary u64 addition fails on overflow, but unused overflow computations may be removed; pub controls verifier-visible input disclosure.
claims.impact: The source-only profile preserves public/private visibility and rejects checked additions that are not live into a final relation assertion, instead of losing overflow through dead-code elimination or unconstrained Field arithmetic.

claims.claim: OpenVM proves execution of a guest compiled through RV32IM ELF/VmExe and offers application, STARK and EVM proof workflows.
claims.impact: OpenVM is a zkVM target with external settlement, not a circuit language or chain contract host.

claims.claim: OpenVM documentation currently spans changing version lines and requires an exact toolchain profile before implementation.
claims.impact: OpenVM is design-only in Phase 1.

claims.claim: Leo 4.0 separates private proof-context fn execution from public finalization-context final execution.
claims.impact: AleoPlan must preserve disclosure and finalization boundaries.

claims.claim: Aleo records and public mappings have different custody and disclosure semantics.
claims.impact: State custody cannot be represented by one generic storage flag.

claims.claim: Psy describes user-partitioned state, local CFC proofs, UPS recursion and network proof aggregation.
claims.impact: Psy is classified as a ZK application chain and needs its own state/settlement plan.

claims.claim: A stable Psy compiler, deploy, proving and network-finalization profile has not been independently reproduced for V2.
claims.impact: Psy remains research-only until a live versioned workflow is verified.

claims.claim: A single target-family enum is insufficient to drive compilation safely.
claims.impact: TargetDescriptor uses orthogonal artifact, execution, commit, state, call, proof, settlement, ABI and resource axes.

claims.claim: Phase 1 implementation scope is EVM, Solana, NEAR and Noir only.
claims.impact: All other dossiers are design/research deliverables and may not advertise an implemented backend.

claims.claim: The new_design directory started without tracked V2 files while the parent repository contains legacy ProofForge modules and target notes.
claims.impact: Create an independent package and use parent observations only through a reference ledger.

claims.claim: Canonical Unicode validation must be pinned to one UCD version and implemented without ambient host normalization libraries.
claims.impact: ProofForge V2 pins Unicode 17.0.0 and uses generated pure-Lean NFC data for canonical wire fields.

claims.claim: The locked V2 development observation contains non-system executable dependency closure and macOS/Xcode-dispatched host tools that cannot be represented by hashing only the top-level executable.
claims.impact: Keep content-addressed assets separate from an attested host profile and fail closed when either closure is incomplete.
